purpose: Narrow novelty audit for a CooperScene transport-availability state contract and frozen-model benchmark-semantics counterfactual. This is not an audit of a new asynchronous compensation network.

directSemanticWorksAdded: Age of Information Guaranteed Scheduling for Asynchronous Status Updates in Collaborative Perception
Timeliness-Oriented Scheduling and Resource Allocation in Multi-Region Collaborative Perception
Learning for V2V Cooperative Perception under Lossy Communication
Bringing Network Coding into Multi-Robot Systems
scope.question: Has prior work already established the exact combination of throughput-and-payload-derived transmission completion, explicit complete/incomplete/right-censored/trace-missing states, and frozen-model counterfactual measurement of fallback-induced benchmark verdict and ranking changes in CooperScene?
outOfScope: A new temporal alignment or asynchronous feature compensation architecture
Claims about unpublished or inaccessible implementations

acceptedEvidence: Primary paper full text from arXiv, CVF Open Access, OpenReview, ACM author-hosted paper, IEEE DOI landing page, or the publisher
Official repository and immutable source-code links where available
evidencePolicy.absenceClaimBoundary: No exact prior was found in the executed public-primary-source search. This is a bounded search result, not a proof that no unpublished, closed-source, patent, or differently named work exists.
evidencePolicy.codeAvailabilityCaveat: Several 2026 papers do not expose a complete public implementation. Paper claims and released-code behavior are therefore kept separate.

candidateDefinition.name: Transport availability state contract for CooperScene replay
candidateDefinition.nonGoal: Do not train or propose another asynchronous compensation network.
systemInput: A directed sender-receiver throughput trace with an explicit unit and sampling interval
The exact runtime serialized payload size for each sender, frame, model, and communication representation
Frame generation time, decision deadline, trace observation interval, and link identity
A frozen perception checkpoint and a fixed underlying scene/frame input

completionEvent.definition: For payload size B_ij bits sent on directed link i->j at t_send, completion is the first t such that the integral of service rate r_ij over [t_send,t] reaches B_ij.
completionEvent.formula: T_complete(i,j,k) = inf{t >= T_send(i,j,k): integral[T_send,t] r_ij(u) du >= 8 * payload_bytes(i,j,k)}
requiredAssumptions: Throughput samples are converted to a stated service-rate unit.
The interpolation rule between samples is fixed, with sample-and-hold and at least one sensitivity alternative reported.
Queue discipline, concurrent payload policy, preemption, and link sharing are explicit.
A payload cannot be declared complete from a scalar mean-throughput division when the proposal claims trace-level completion semantics.

availabilityStates.definition: The intended source-frame payload completed by the decision deadline.
The intended source-frame payload did not complete by the deadline, but at least one older payload completed and is available; its age is explicit.
The payload has not completed by the decision deadline, while the trace continues far enough to determine a later completion or continued service.
A payload has not completed when the observable service trace ends, so only a lower bound on completion time is known.
The directed link, interval, unit, timestamp alignment, or required throughput sample is absent or invalid; transport availability is not identifiable and must fail closed.

boundaryClarification.deadlineNonCompletionIsNotAutomaticallyR: If the trace continues after the deadline, the payload is incomplete at the deadline but not right-censored merely because the benchmark made a decision.
boundaryClarification.takeStartIsNotRightCensoring: A request for history before the beginning of a take is left-truncated or warm-start-unknown. Calling the silent first-frame clamp right-censoring would be statistically incorrect.
boundaryClarification.dropIsAPolicyNotAState: Drop is one action after an unavailable or expired message state is established; it is not evidence about why the message is unavailable.
boundaryClarification.expirationIsAPolicyNotCompletion: A completed but stale payload may be expired, while an unfinished payload may never have become available. These cases must remain distinguishable.

counterfactualPolicies.definition: Reproduce the audited public CooperScene behavior when requested history exceeds the take.
Exclude the unavailable collaborator payload from fusion without substituting another frame.
Fuse only the newest payload whose completion event precedes the decision deadline, with its age recorded.
Use a frozen model's existing, documented delay/age input with the completion-derived age. Mark this policy unsupported for models without a native age input rather than adding a learned adapter.

auditedCooperSceneFacts.finding: The audited public dataset path derives a scalar delay from payload size divided by throughput and discretizes it into frame delay.
auditedCooperSceneFacts.implication: The public path models delay but does not expose a transport completion state machine.

auditedCooperSceneFacts.finding: When requested delay exceeds available history, delayed lookup clamps to the first frame.
auditedCooperSceneFacts.implication: The first frame can be silently treated as if it were a valid delayed message even when no such historical completion is established.

auditedCooperSceneFacts.finding: When delayed lookup returns no sample, the already loaded synchronized collaborator entry can remain in the sample.
auditedCooperSceneFacts.implication: A failed delayed lookup can preserve current synchronized information instead of making unavailability explicit.

auditedCooperSceneFacts.finding: The cooperative detector initializes prior_encoding.time_delay to zero, and the audited dataset path does not thread the computed delay into this field.
auditedCooperSceneFacts.implication: An age-aware model path can receive a zero-delay prior even when the dataset selected a delayed frame.

auditedCooperSceneFacts.finding: The released communication trace exposes directed throughput samples but not packet events, latency, loss, jitter, retransmission, or queue state.
auditedCooperSceneFacts.implication: Completion can only be derived under an explicit service model; packet-level ground-truth claims are prohibited.

taxonomy.definition: A method aligns, predicts, or warps an already selected stale feature or message using an assumed/configured delay.
taxonomy.distinguishingQuestion: How should an available stale message be compensated?
taxonomy.notEquivalentBecause: It does not by itself determine whether a payload completed and became available.

taxonomy.definition: A system replays recorded or configured network conditions during evaluation.
taxonomy.distinguishingQuestion: How are time-varying network conditions reproduced?
taxonomy.notEquivalentBecause: Replay can still use ambiguous completion, fallback, warm-start, or missing-trace semantics.

taxonomy.definition: A policy rejects a message after a staleness or deadline rule.
taxonomy.distinguishingQuestion: What should happen to a late or stale message?
taxonomy.notEquivalentBecause: Expiration does not identify whether the message was complete, unfinished, lost, or unobservable.

taxonomy.definition: A system fuses only messages that arrive before a decision deadline and may select a fallback for missing views.
taxonomy.distinguishingQuestion: Which arrived messages may enter this decision?
taxonomy.notEquivalentBecause: It is a strong functional collision for availability-at-deadline, but published systems do not provide the proposed CooperScene-specific right-censoring and trace-missing benchmark counterfactual.

taxonomy.definition: The observation window ends before completion is observed, while a lower bound on completion time remains known.
taxonomy.distinguishingQuestion: Is completion absent, or merely unobserved beyond the trace boundary?
taxonomy.notEquivalentBecause: No directly matching cooperative-perception primary work was found that uses this explicit transport-observation state in benchmark replay.

taxonomy.definition: A deterministic, auditable mapping from trace evidence and payload service to availability state, model input, and fallback action.
taxonomy.distinguishingQuestion: What evidence makes each message available, unavailable, censored, or unidentifiable, and how does that state affect the benchmark verdict?
taxonomy.notEquivalentBecause: It treats data-state semantics and benchmark validity as the object of study rather than treating delay as an input corruption alone.

coreClaims.claim: A CooperScene replay should expose current-complete, historical-complete, incomplete-at-deadline, right-censored, and trace-missing-or-invalid states instead of silently converting all cases to a frame index.
coreClaims.noveltyBoundary: The state taxonomy is not novel merely because it uses deadlines or drops. Its defensible contribution is the explicit observation contract tied to CooperScene's directed throughput and runtime payload.

coreClaims.claim: Under frozen checkpoints and identical underlying scenes, fallback policy alone can be isolated as a benchmark-semantic variable.
coreClaims.noveltyBoundary: Harbor and CoInfra already implement deadline-aware missing-view behavior. The narrower delta is a controlled counterfactual over silent clamp, drop, latest completed, and model-native age handling on the same completed-message ledger.

coreClaims.claim: Benchmark verdict sensitivity should be measured both as metric change and as method-ordering stability.
coreClaims.noveltyBoundary: V2X-ReaLO already demonstrates that online execution can change performance relative to offline evaluation. The candidate must measure attribution to availability semantics rather than claim the first online/offline ranking discrepancy.

coreClaims.claim: A pre-registered equivalence result can justify a simpler availability contract over the released trace support.
coreClaims.noveltyBoundary: A non-significant difference is insufficient. Simplification evidence requires state-frequency coverage, equivalence margins, and confidence intervals.

coreClaims.claim: The audited CooperScene public path contains silent first-frame clamp, synchronized-frame retention on failed delayed lookup, and a zero-valued time-delay prior path.
coreClaims.noveltyBoundary: These are code-audit findings and motivation. They are not by themselves a standalone research contribution.

closestPriorWork.work: Harbor: Boosting Collaborative Vehicular Perception on the Edge with V2V Communication
closestPriorWork.occupiedFunction: Trace-driven network emulation, a 500 ms end-to-end deadline, local fallback when the edge result misses the deadline, and an edge-result bitmap identifying which vehicle views were processed so missing views can be merged locally.
closestPriorWork.remainingDelta: No CooperScene directed-throughput completion ledger, no explicit right-censored versus trace-missing states, and no frozen-model four-policy ranking-stability audit.

closestPriorWork.work: CoInfra: A Communication-Aware Cooperative Perception System for CAVs
closestPriorWork.occupiedFunction: Trace-driven synchronization, adaptive deadlines, fusion of only messages that arrive before the deadline, and substitution of missing expected contributions using the most recent observation and EKF prediction.
closestPriorWork.remainingDelta: The proposed contract distinguishes incomplete, censored, and trace-missing evidence and audits CooperScene verdict sensitivity without introducing a new predictor.
closestPriorWork.codeCaveat: The indexed official repository did not expose the paper's deadline, latency-trace, or EKF logic in searchable source at audit time; system claims are therefore paper-supported, not code-verified.

closestPriorWork.work: V2X-ReaLO: An Open Online Framework and Dataset for Cooperative Perception
closestPriorWork.occupiedFunction: Real online ROS transmission, serialization and compression measurements, a receiver feature bank, selection of the latest collaborator neural message within a time window, and evidence that offline and online conclusions can differ.
closestPriorWork.remainingDelta: It does not publish the proposed completion/censoring/trace-missing state contract or isolate fallback semantics on one frozen completed-message ledger.
closestPriorWork.codeCaveat: The paper states that code and data will be released; no official repository was verified in this audit.

closestPriorWork.work: CooperScene: A Large-scale Comprehensive Dataset and Benchmark for Cooperative Perception
closestPriorWork.occupiedFunction: Dataset, benchmark, communication traces, scalar payload/throughput delay conversion, delayed-frame lookup, and a model prior encoding with a time-delay slot.
closestPriorWork.remainingDelta: The public path does not expose the proposed state contract, runtime per-message completion ledger, fail-closed trace-missing behavior, or policy counterfactual.

closestPriorWork.work: CADET: A System and Benchmarking Toolkit for Collaborative Autonomous Driving Systems
closestPriorWork.occupiedFunction: Trace-driven network and workload emulation with synchronized model, system, and task metrics; the paper describes replayable latency, jitter, loss, and bandwidth profiles.
closestPriorWork.remainingDelta: It is a general systems benchmark rather than the proposed CooperScene-specific completion/censoring contract and frozen fallback-semantics audit.
closestPriorWork.codeCaveat: The official GitHub repository was empty through the GitHub API at audit time, so implementation semantics could not be verified.

closestPriorWork.work: RCP-Bench: Benchmarking Robustness for Collaborative Perception under Diverse Corruptions
closestPriorWork.occupiedFunction: A robustness benchmark in which RCP-Drop randomly discards collaborator data to simulate sensor or communication failures, alongside temporal misalignment and other corruptions.
closestPriorWork.remainingDelta: Random drop is a corruption operator, not a completion event or censoring state inferred from directed throughput and runtime payload.

closestPriorWork.work: V2X-INCOP: A Communication-Resilient Cooperative Perception Framework
closestPriorWork.occupiedFunction: Models random communication interruption and uses historical information with a learned spatiotemporal mechanism to recover missing collaborator messages.
closestPriorWork.remainingDelta: It treats interruption as a communication corruption and learns recovery; it does not distinguish unfinished, right-censored, and trace-missing states or run a frozen fallback-semantics audit.

closestPriorWork.work: LRCP: Latency Robust Cooperative Perception using Asynchronous Feature Fusion
closestPriorWork.occupiedFunction: Uses cached historical BEV features and explicit delay inputs to compensate asynchronous feature fusion, with configured delay evaluation.
closestPriorWork.remainingDelta: It assumes a stale feature has been selected and does not infer whether transport completed or distinguish missing trace from unfinished service.

closestPriorWork.work: TraF-Align: Trajectory-aware Feature Alignment for Asynchronous Multi-agent Perception
closestPriorWork.occupiedFunction: Aligns asynchronous multi-agent features using trajectory cues; the official configuration simulates delay and threads time_delay into the model.
closestPriorWork.remainingDelta: Configured delay augmentation and feature alignment do not define transport completion or observation censoring.

closestPriorWork.work: CATNet: Collaborative Alignment and Transformation Network for Cooperative Perception
closestPriorWork.occupiedFunction: STSync aligns asynchronous feature streams through adjacent-frame differential modeling, alongside denoising and feature selection.
closestPriorWork.remainingDelta: It addresses feature degradation after asynchronous input selection, not evidence for message completion, censoring, or trace failure.
closestPriorWork.codeCaveat: No official public code repository was verified in this audit.

closestPriorWork.work: CooperTrim: Toward Adaptive Feature Selection for Resource-Efficient Collaborative Perception
closestPriorWork.occupiedFunction: Adaptively changes requested feature quantity using temporal uncertainty and scene complexity, creating model- and frame-dependent communication payloads.
closestPriorWork.remainingDelta: It determines what and how much to request, not whether a selected runtime payload completed by a decision deadline or became censored.

closestPriorWork.work: AdaMap: High-scalable Real-time Cooperative Perception at the Edge
closestPriorWork.occupiedFunction: Adapts object selection and compression under time-varying networking to meet percentile-latency objectives.
closestPriorWork.remainingDelta: It optimizes payload and latency rather than auditing distinct completion-observation states and benchmark fallback bias.

closestPriorWork.work: Age of Information Guaranteed Scheduling for Asynchronous Status Updates in Collaborative Perception
closestPriorWork.occupiedFunction: Formulates asynchronous collaborative-perception scheduling with Age of Information constraints.
closestPriorWork.remainingDelta: AoI scheduling controls update freshness but does not provide the proposed data-lineage states or frozen fallback-policy counterfactual.

closestPriorWork.work: Timeliness-Oriented Scheduling and Resource Allocation in Multi-Region Collaborative Perception
closestPriorWork.occupiedFunction: Jointly treats timeliness, communication volume, scheduling, and resource allocation for collaborative perception.
closestPriorWork.remainingDelta: It optimizes when and how much to communicate, not the replay semantics of incomplete and censored messages in an existing benchmark.

closestPriorWork.work: Learning for V2V Cooperative Perception under Lossy Communication
closestPriorWork.occupiedFunction: Learns cooperative perception under lossy communication and repairs corrupted transmitted features.
closestPriorWork.remainingDelta: Lossy packet repair is distinct from determining whether a whole runtime payload completed by a deadline or was right-censored by trace termination.

closestPriorWork.work: Bringing Network Coding into Multi-Robot Systems: A Practical Case for Coping with Lossy Wireless Links
closestPriorWork.occupiedFunction: Studies delayed and lossy transport, in-order delivery stalls, and deadline reliability for safety-relevant V2V messages.
closestPriorWork.remainingDelta: It is transport-adjacent but does not audit cooperative-perception model rankings or CooperScene fallback semantics.

closestPriorWork.work: STARE: Bridging the latency gap in continuous stream evaluation
closestPriorWork.occupiedFunction: Evaluates continuous predictions against high-frequency ground truth using the latest available prediction and explicitly treats output staleness as an evaluation concern.
closestPriorWork.remainingDelta: It is not collaborative perception and does not model directed wireless payload completion, but it is a direct warning against claiming that availability-aware benchmark semantics are conceptually unprecedented.

functionalEquivalenceCollisions.equivalentFunction: Determine whether a collaborative result or contributing view is present by a deadline and invoke an explicit local fallback.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.severityForNovelty: This occupies the broad claim of first deadline-aware availability and fallback in collaborative vehicular perception.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.survivingDifference: The candidate audits a released benchmark's hidden fallback semantics with throughput-derived completion, censoring, trace-missing states, and cross-policy ranking stability.

functionalEquivalenceCollisions.equivalentFunction: Fuse only messages that arrive before an adaptive deadline and replace missing expected contributions using the most recent observation plus prediction.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.severityForNovelty: This occupies deadline-aware message-set construction and latest-history substitution.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.survivingDifference: The candidate has no learned predictor and asks whether benchmark conclusions change solely because the availability-state contract changes.

functionalEquivalenceCollisions.equivalentFunction: Use actual online message arrival behavior, retain received neural messages in a feature bank, and select the latest message within a time window.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.severityForNovelty: This occupies the broad claim that online availability and stale-message selection matter to cooperative-perception evaluation.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.survivingDifference: The candidate formalizes unavailable versus censored versus unidentifiable states and compares fallback policies on the same completion ledger.

functionalEquivalenceCollisions.equivalentFunction: Represent communication failure by dropping or recovering collaborator information.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.severityForNovelty: This occupies generic drop robustness and missing-message recovery.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.survivingDifference: The candidate does not treat all absence as Bernoulli drop; it assigns evidence-grounded states before applying a policy.

functionalEquivalenceCollisions.equivalentFunction: Replay time-varying network conditions and correlate them with system or task outcomes.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.survivingDifference: The candidate's narrow object is the semantics of transmission completion and observation boundaries in CooperScene, not trace replay itself.

functionalEquivalenceCollisions.equivalentFunction: Use message age or delay to compensate asynchronous features.
functionalEquivalenceCollisions.survivingDifference: The candidate only feeds completion-derived age into an already existing native path and freezes all weights.

explicitDelta.oneSentence: The defensible delta is a CooperScene-specific, evidence-typed transport availability contract plus a frozen-model counterfactual that attributes benchmark verdict and ranking changes to fallback semantics rather than to a newly trained compensation method.
elementsThatMustAppearTogether: Exact runtime serialized payload size rather than a nominal tensor-size constant
Directed trace integration rather than a scalar mean-throughput delay
An auditable completion ledger with stated service and queue assumptions
Separate current-complete, historical-complete, incomplete-at-deadline, right-censored, and trace-missing-or-invalid states
Correct treatment of take-start warmup as left-truncated or unknown rather than right-censored
Frozen checkpoints and fixed underlying scenes across policy counterfactuals
Silent first-frame clamp, drop, latest-completed, and supported model-native age-aware policies
Both metric/verdict sensitivity and method-ordering stability
A pre-specified equivalence analysis for negative results
whatIsNotDelta: Discovering that online and offline metrics differ
The CooperScene code bug report by itself
explicitDelta.boundedNoveltyFinding: No audited 2023-2026 primary source combined all required elements. Harbor and CoInfra are the closest functional collisions and materially narrow the claim.

notViableAs: A paper whose only contribution is fixing first-frame clamp
conditionsForIndependentProject: The affected states occur often enough across released traces, payloads, and model operating points to support inference beyond a few take-boundary frames.
At least several heterogeneous frozen methods are evaluated, including native age-aware and non-age-aware methods.
Harbor-style deadline/drop fallback and CoInfra-style latest-history fallback are acknowledged and operationally represented in the comparison.
The study reports a formal estimand: policy-induced change in metric, pairwise method verdict, and ranking under a shared completion ledger.
Completion assumptions and their sensitivity materially affect or tightly bound conclusions.
Negative results use equivalence margins and state-coverage evidence rather than a failure to reject a null.
The artifact is reusable as an evaluator, ledger, tests, and state-level diagnostics rather than a one-off patch.
standaloneProjectAssessment.collapseCondition: If almost all samples are current-complete, differences are confined to warm-start frames, and ranking/verdict equivalence holds under all plausible service assumptions, the work should be presented as a benchmark contract note or merged into a broader trace-replay study.

strongestObjections.objection: Harbor and CoInfra already implement the core systems idea of deadline-aware message/view availability plus explicit fallback.
strongestObjections.requiredResponse: Claim only the CooperScene-specific completion-observation contract and frozen benchmark counterfactual; reproduce those prior policy classes rather than portraying them as new.

strongestObjections.objection: Right-censoring may be terminology without a statistical estimand or method.
strongestObjections.requiredResponse: Define the observation boundary, preserve completion-time lower bounds, separate deadline noncompletion from trace-end censoring, and show how state treatment changes estimands, inclusion, or uncertainty.

strongestObjections.objection: Directed throughput plus payload size does not identify packet loss, retransmission, queuing, MAC contention, or application-level delivery.
strongestObjections.requiredResponse: Call the result throughput-derived service completion, publish queue/interpolation assumptions, and run sensitivity analyses. Do not claim measured network delivery.

strongestObjections.objection: The first-frame clamp may affect only take warmup and therefore be too rare for a standalone result.
strongestObjections.requiredResponse: Report state prevalence before headline accuracy, stratify warmup versus steady state, and apply the collapse condition if support is negligible.

strongestObjections.objection: Ranking changes may be caused by architecture-specific payload size rather than fallback semantics.
strongestObjections.requiredResponse: Report both actual-payload and equalized-payload controls, and decompose transport-load effects from policy effects.

strongestObjections.objection: An age-aware-native policy is not comparable for models that do not accept age, and adding an adapter would violate the frozen-model design.
strongestObjections.requiredResponse: Use native inputs only where documented, declare unsupported cells, and keep drop/latest-completed comparisons common across all methods.

strongestObjections.objection: Trace missing is data quality, while unfinished transport is a physical state; putting both in one ordinal state variable can imply false ordering.
strongestObjections.requiredResponse: Use a tagged union or separate availability and observability fields. Trace-missing must fail closed and remain excluded from transport-performance claims.

strongestObjections.objection: A frozen-model comparison changes collaborator inputs across policies, so 'same input' can be misleading.
strongestObjections.requiredResponse: State that the underlying ego frame, candidate collaborator frames, trace, payload, and checkpoint are fixed; the fused collaborator set and age metadata are the controlled intervention.

strongestObjections.objection: Frames within a take and directed links are not independent, making naive confidence intervals and rank tests anti-conservative.
strongestObjections.requiredResponse: Use take-clustered or hierarchical resampling and report take-level effects.

strongestObjections.objection: A negative result can be misrepresented as evidence that semantics never matter.
strongestObjections.requiredResponse: Predefine practical equivalence margins and limit simplification claims to the audited traces, payload range, deadlines, models, and state frequencies.

necessaryExperiments.question: Does the completion ledger implement the stated transport evidence correctly?
requirements: Unit tests for exact-boundary completion, partial service, zero throughput, missing directed link, trace end, take start, and concurrent payload assumptions.
Independent numerical integration cross-check on sampled links.
Per-state counts and durations before any perception result.

necessaryExperiments.question: Can the audited CooperScene fallback behavior be reproduced and isolated?
requirements: A test where requested delay exceeds available history and selects the first frame.
A test where delayed lookup is missing and the synchronized collaborator remains.
A test showing whether completion-derived delay reaches prior_encoding.time_delay.
Byte-for-byte or tensor-identity logging of the collaborator input under each policy.

necessaryExperiments.question: Are conclusions robust to plausible interpretations of the released throughput trace?
requirements: Sample-and-hold versus an alternative interpolation.
FIFO serialization versus explicitly bounded concurrency assumptions.
Actual runtime payload versus nominal and equalized payload controls.
Multiple decision deadlines and warmup policies.

necessaryExperiments.question: How much does fallback semantics alone change outputs?
requirements: Freeze checkpoint, preprocessing, ego frame, candidate collaborator frames, trace segment, payload encoding, and random seed.
Change only silent clamp, drop, latest-completed, or supported native age-aware policy.
Store paired per-frame detections and state lineage.

necessaryExperiments.question: Do policy changes alter benchmark conclusions or method ordering?
requirements: Report primary task metrics and paired deltas.
Report pairwise winner sign, top-method agreement, rank inversions, Kendall tau, and Spearman rho.
Use take-clustered confidence intervals.
Predefine what constitutes a benchmark verdict change.

necessaryExperiments.question: Which availability states drive any observed effect?
requirements: Separate current-complete, historical-complete, incomplete-at-deadline, right-censored, trace-missing, and take-start-unknown cases.
Report warmup and steady-state results separately.
Relate effect size to payload, directed throughput, collaborator count, and message age without treating correlated frames as independent.

necessaryExperiments.question: Does the candidate improve semantic precision beyond the closest prior policy classes?
requirements: Harbor-style deadline/drop or local-only fallback.
CoInfra-style latest-history fallback, without claiming its EKF predictor is reproduced unless it actually is.
V2X-ReaLO-style latest-in-window selection.
RCP-Bench-style random drop as a corruption control rather than a transport-ground-truth baseline.

necessaryExperiments.question: When may the contract be simplified?
requirements: Pre-register practical equivalence margins for task metric and ranking stability.
Use confidence intervals compatible with clustered data.
Require adequate exposure to non-current-complete states.
State the exact trace, payload, deadline, and model support over which simplification is justified.

negativeResultContract.acceptableInference: Within the audited support and pre-specified margins, a simpler fallback policy is practically equivalent to the fuller state contract for the evaluated benchmark verdict.
negativeResultContract.unacceptableInference: Availability semantics do not matter in cooperative perception.
minimumEvidence: No hidden replacement of missing trace with zero delay or first-frame data

allowedClaims: We audit a CooperScene-specific transport-availability contract derived from released directed throughput and exact runtime payload under explicit service assumptions.
We distinguish completion at a decision deadline, later-observed incompletion, trace-end right-censoring, take-start unknown history, and missing or invalid trace evidence.
We isolate fallback semantics with frozen checkpoints and fixed underlying scene/trace inputs.
We quantify how silent first-frame clamp, drop, latest-completed, and supported native age-aware handling affect benchmark metrics, verdicts, and method-ordering stability.
In the executed 2023-2026 primary-source search, no work was found that combines this exact CooperScene completion-state contract with the proposed frozen-policy counterfactual.
Harbor and CoInfra are the closest functional precedents for deadline-aware availability and fallback.
A negative equivalence result can support a simpler contract only within the measured trace, payload, deadline, state-frequency, and model range.
forbiddenClaims: The first work on message availability, deadlines, missing views, or fallback in cooperative perception.
The first trace-driven collaborative-perception benchmark or system.
The first work to select the latest available or historical collaborator message.
The first work to show online and offline cooperative-perception results differ.
The first asynchronous or latency-robust cooperative-perception method.
The released CooperScene trace measures packet latency, packet loss, jitter, retransmission, or MAC behavior.
Throughput divided into payload size is measured end-to-end delivery latency.
A payload incomplete at the benchmark deadline is necessarily right-censored.
A request before take start is right-censored.
Drop, expiration, trace missing, and unfinished transmission are equivalent states.
Silent first-frame clamp causes benchmark bias or rank inversion before paired experiments establish it.
A lack of statistical significance proves fallback policies are equivalent.
The findings generalize to all radios, deployments, datasets, payload formats, or deadlines.
The contribution is a new compensation architecture when all model weights are frozen.
Public-code behavior was verified for CADET, CATNet, or V2X-ReaLO when no inspectable implementation was available.

queryFamilies.intent: Resolve each required work to its primary paper, formal page, project, and official code.
Find cooperative-perception work that explicitly determines whether a collaborator message or view is available at a decision time.
Find work distinguishing in-flight or incomplete payloads from loss, drop, and stale completed messages.
Find cooperative-perception work using right-censored completion observations or trace-boundary semantics.
Find first-frame clamp, local-only, drop, latest-arrived, latest-completed, and predicted-history fallback behavior.
Separate deadline-aware message selection and packet/message expiration from completion observation.
Find trace-driven evaluation systems and determine whether their trace use implies an explicit availability contract.
Find online, streaming, or network-aware benchmarks that report changes in model conclusions or ranking.

searchAudit.directSearchResult: Harbor, CoInfra, and V2X-ReaLO provide the closest availability/fallback functions. No primary source in the executed search exposed the exact combination of CooperScene directed-throughput plus runtime-payload completion, explicit incomplete/right-censored/trace-missing states, and frozen fallback-policy ranking counterfactual.
specificNoMatchObservations: No directly matching cooperative-perception primary work was found for the phrase and concept of right-censored transmission completion.
No directly matching public implementation was found for explicit first-frame-clamp semantics as an intentional benchmark contract.

Prior work does directly cover deadline-aware arrival sets, local fallback, latest-history substitution, random drop, lossy repair, trace replay, and age-aware compensation; these are not novelty gaps.
limitations: The search is limited to public sources available on 2026-07-31.
Closed, proprietary, unpublished, and patent sources were not audited.
CADET's official repository was empty at audit time.
No official public code was verified for CATNet or V2X-ReaLO.
The audit did not execute full training or benchmark pipelines.

conclusion.answer: The candidate can be an independent narrow project only when framed as benchmark validity and transport-semantics measurement, with Harbor and CoInfra treated as strong functional precedents. The exact proposed combination was not found, but most broad component claims are already occupied.
conclusion.mostDefensibleContribution: An executable CooperScene completion-and-observability contract, paired frozen-policy counterfactuals, state-stratified verdict/ranking analysis, and equivalence-based negative-result simplification.
conclusion.mainNoveltyRisk: Reviewers may view the work as a benchmark bug fix or a repackaging of Harbor/CoInfra deadline fallback unless the censoring distinction, shared completion ledger, causal policy isolation, and cross-method verdict stability are all central and experimentally consequential.
conclusion.goNoGoGate: Before full-scale evaluation, run state-prevalence and warmup-versus-steady-state diagnostics. If non-current states are negligible or only boundary artifacts, merge the work into a broader CooperScene replay audit rather than claiming a standalone method contribution.
